_activity: Which principle, by its card name?
intro: Pick the best one. Hints are here if you want them.

items.stem: Which principle is at stake in Document 7, Worcester v. Georgia?

options.1: Federalism — Georgia's laws can have no force on Cherokee land, so valid federal treaties win
options.2: Due Process — the Cherokee were given fair steps before their land was taken from them
options.3: Separation of Powers — the Court, Congress and the President each had their own job to do
options.4: Popular Sovereignty — Georgia's voters wanted the land, and government rules with their agreement

hints: The card says power is divided between the national government and the states.
What does Marshall say about whose law applies on Cherokee land?
items.reason: Marshall holds that Georgia's law has no force where federal treaties govern, which is Federalism on the card: when the two clash, valid federal law wins. Judicial Review also fits this document and is accepted.

items.stem: Which principle is at stake in Document 11, the Declaration of Sentiments?

options.1: Representative Government — women had no voice in making the laws they had to obey
options.2: Limited Government — the Constitution did not allow the government to do what it did
options.3: Checks and Balances — one branch of the government blocked or limited the others
options.4: Rule of Law — no one is above the law, not even the people who make it

hints: The document says she was compelled to obey laws “in the formation of which she had no voice.”
Which card name is about electing the people who make decisions for you?
items.reason: The Declaration's complaint is that women were denied the vote and so had no representation — Representative Government, denied. Popular Sovereignty and Equal Protection also fit this document and are accepted.

items.stem: Which principle is at stake in Document 1, Jefferson's letter?

options.1: Limited Government — Jefferson wrote the Constitution “has made no provision” for holding foreign territory
options.2: Judicial Review — a court struck down the treaty because it broke the Constitution
options.3: Equal Protection — the law treated the people of Louisiana exactly the same as everyone
options.4: Individual Rights — the government could not take away freedom of speech or religion

hints: The card says government can only do what the Constitution allows.
No court appears anywhere in this document.
items.reason: Jefferson's whole problem is that the Constitution does not authorise what he is doing, which is Limited Government — and the document shows it being fought over, since he goes ahead anyway. No court is involved, so Judicial Review cannot be it.
